Trying to understand a little in the thought process on why this would go into platform init.  CMOS clear is an action that happens long after init, so significantly changes how platform-init works.  Any discussion of this in your commit message would be appreciated.

To be more clear here, I'm not against this, I would just like to see some discussion about why this repo is a logical place to put this feature.  The initial design doc for platform-init intentionally only covered init, ie the startup things the controller needs to do on launch.  It didn't cover runtime, and dbus was explicitly discounted.

I'm open to adding these things, would just like to see some amount of justification (like would go in a design doc) about why this is the best path.

I provided additional info in the commit message.

I agree, this changes platform-init from how it is documented. If we find agreement on this I would update the doc with the relevant information.

To pick up the conversation you and @patrick@stwcx.xyz had in the previous patch: 

The reason I went with a second binary was mainly due to the fact how the init subcommand and the reset service functionally diverge. While `init` is calling a one-shot function, the reset service spawns an async dbus service with the provided reset function. Doing it this way felt cleaner to me, but I might be wrong. On the other hand it currently adds slightly more overhead on the yocto side and more importantly might be misaligned with already documented designs.

I am fine expanding on the `platform` binary instead and adding a secondary subcommand.
I have updated the series to execute from a subcommand instead of a separate binary. I'll follow-up with a design doc update to continue the discussion there.

I have update the doc: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/91324. 
Closing this thread as I am expecting to continue the conversation in 91324.
